dedupe_keys.name: the effects of nearby trees on the positional accuracy of gnss receivers in a forest environment lee et al plos one 2023

description: This 2023 PLOS ONE study measured the positional accuracy of three GNSS receivers, a Garmin and a Trimble handheld unit and a smartphone, at 26 control points at the Whitehall Forest GPS test site in Athens, Georgia. Thirty-five forest variables describing the size and location of vegetation around each control point were correlated with horizontal position error. The smartphone had significantly lower error than the Garmin receiver and a similar but significantly different error from the Trimble, correlations between forest variables and error were significant but their trends were not consistent, and the location of nearby trees mattered more than their size. Producer: University of Georgia forestry researchers, published 15 March 2023. Coverage: one forest test site. Access: full text open on PubMed Central. Licence and cost: free; the article states a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: one site, three receivers and a small number of control points, and whether the measurements are downloadable was not confirmed. Simulation uses: it provides measured error against vegetation variables to validate GNSS multipath and canopy attenuation models. Related record: mesh radio connectivity models using forest vegetation, lidar and satellite data (model-mesh-radio-connectivity-forest-vegetation-lidar-satellite-models).
